newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices continue climb on heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices continue climb on heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to strengthen Wednesday with the unrelenting heat across most of the U.S. and inflated electricity prices, sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about two to three cents higher at $2.23-2.24 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.
Similarly in south Texas prices gained three cents to about $2.17-2.18 as temperature highs hovered around 100 degrees F.
In the Permian Basin market, prices rose another two cents to $2.13-2.16, while southern California border prices were up an equal amount to the high-$2.20s.

Tempering a larger increase was news that both the San Onofre nuclear units had restarted. The 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 was expected to reconnect to the grid today, while the adjacent unit 3, rated at 1,080 MW, was expected to resume power output Thursday.
San Juan prices firmed to about $2.10-2.15, while Waha values edged to about $2.17.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico was still off line for another two and a half weeks of repairs.

In the Midwest, swing prices gained another two cents to about $2.10-2.13. Chicago city-gate prices, however, were quoted unchanged in the high-$2.20s despite highs still in the 90s F. Cooler weather is forecast for the area this weekend.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate also strengthened to the mid-to-high $2.50s.
